Feluda.description: A private detective renowned for his sharp intellect and deductive skills, often addressed respectfully as Felu Babu.

Dinanath Lahiri.description: A client with sharp observational skills who approaches Feluda regarding an exchanged attaché case containing a valuable manuscript.

Mr Pakrashi.description: A Bengali businessman and fellow passenger on the Kalka Mail who was potentially involved in the attaché case mix-up.

Srinath.description: The cook in Feluda's household, who serves tea during the meeting.

Shambhucharan Bose.description: Author of a 1917 travelogue about Tibet, whose manuscript was in the lost attaché case; mentioned as someone who was close to Dinanath Babu's uncle, possibly a fellow shikari.

Satinath Lahiri.description: Dinanath Lahiri's uncle, a former tutor in Kathmandu, to whom the Tibet travelogue was dedicated.

Captain Scott.description: Reference to Robert Falcon Scott, the British explorer known for his expeditions to the Antarctic.

Tara Road.description: The street where Feluda's house is located.

Rolls-Royce.description: A luxury British car brand, used here to describe the impressive size of the visitor's car.

Hispano Suiza.description: A rare and prestigious European luxury car brand, owned by Dinanath Lahiri.

Kalka Mail.description: A famous Indian train running between Delhi and Howrah.

Delhi.description: India's capital city, from where the train journey began.

Simla.description: A hill station in northern India, now known as Shimla.

Kathmandu.description: The capital city of Nepal, where Satinath Lahiri once lived.

Ranas.description: A prominent ruling family in Nepal, historically known for their political power; referenced as the hereditary prime ministers of Nepal and as the giver of the diamond.

Nepali.description: Relating to Nepal; here, it refers to a box from Nepal.

Pest Control.description: A service for removing pests, mentioned in the context of cleaning out the box room.

Makaibari.description: A renowned tea estate in Kurseong, known for its high-quality tea.

Kurseong.description: A hill station in West Bengal, famous for its tea plantations.

Kodak.description: A famous brand of photographic film and related products.

Calcutta.description: The former name of Kolkata, a major city in eastern India.

Howrah.description: A city adjacent to Kolkata, known for its major railway station.

Chowringhee.description: A central area in Kolkata, known for its historical and commercial significance.

Park Street.description: A well-known street in Kolkata, famous for its restaurants and nightlife.

Hindustan Times.description: A major English-language daily newspaper in India.

Binaca.description: A popular brand of toothpaste and toothbrushes in India.

Gillette.description: A global brand known for razors and shaving products.

Old Spice.description: A well-known brand of men's grooming products.

Venus.description: A brand of pencils, here referring to a red-and-blue pencil.

Moradabad.description: A city in Uttar Pradesh, India, famous for its brassware and handicrafts.

Ellery Queen.description: A famous fictional detective and the pseudonym of the authors who created him.

The Door Between.description: A detective novel by Ellery Queen.

dhoti.description: A traditional Indian men's garment, a long piece of cloth wrapped around the waist and legs.

kurta.description: A loose, collarless shirt worn in South Asia.

nagra.description: A type of traditional Indian footwear, often with an upturned toe.

attaché case.description: A small, flat, rectangular suitcase used for carrying documents.

Baba.description: A respectful term for father in many Indian languages.

Babu.description: A term of respect or endearment for men in India, often used after a name; in this context, used as an honorific for Feluda (Felu Babu), Lalmohan Ganguly (Lalmohan Babu), and Naresh Chandra Pakrashi (Naresh Babu).

betel-nut.description: The seed(s) of the areca palm, commonly chewed in South and Southeast Asia for their stimulant effects.

pukka sahib.description: A term from colonial India meaning a true gentleman, often used to describe someone with British manners.

thali.description: A traditional Indian meal served on a round platter, consisting of various dishes.

Uncle Sidhu.description: A knowledgeable and respected family friend of Feluda and the narrator, known for his extraordinary memory.

Brijmohan.description: A moneylender who traveled in the same compartment as Mr Lahiri and Mr Pakrashi.

Dasgupta.description: A Bengali receptionist at the Grand Hotel who assists Feluda and the narrator.

Terai.description: A region at the base of the Himalayas, referenced as the subject of Shambhucharan Bose's travel book.

Nepal.description: A country in South Asia, ruled by the Ranas during the period described.

Vijayendra Shamsher Jung Bahadur.description: A member of the Rana family in Nepal, known for his hunting exploits.

National Library.description: A major library, likely referring to the National Library of India in Kolkata.

Lansdowne Road.description: A street in Kolkata where Naresh Chandra Pakrashi lives.

Lenin Sarani.description: A major road in Kolkata, location of S. M. Kedia & Co.

S. M. Kedia & Co..description: A company associated with Brijmohan, the moneylender, and visited by Feluda during his investigation.

Lower Circular Road.description: A street in Kolkata, site of a recent robbery.

Ambassador.description: A classic Indian car, mentioned as the getaway vehicle in the robbery.

Hindustan International Hotel.description: A prominent hotel in Kolkata visited by Feluda during the investigation.

Park Hotel.description: A well-known hotel in Kolkata, checked by Feluda for the guest from Simla.

Ritz Continental.description: A hotel in Kolkata, one of the five mentioned by Feluda.

Wild Flower Hall.description: A famous hotel and historic building near Simla, formerly a residence during British times and part of G. C. Dhameeja's address.

The Nook.description: The name of the residence or suite at Wild Flower Hall, Simla.

shikari.description: A hunter, especially one who hunts big game in India.

machan.description: A platform built on a tree or raised structure, used for hunting or watching animals.

almirahs.description: Cupboards or wardrobes, commonly used in Indian households.

rexine.description: A type of artificial leather often used for covering furniture.

guru.description: A spiritual teacher or guide in Indian religions.

applewalla.description: A colloquial term for a person associated with apples; 'walla' is a suffix denoting someone involved with a particular thing.

Charminar.description: A popular Indian brand of cigarettes.

Amar Kumar.description: Dinanath Babu's nephew and an aspiring actor who used the screen name Amar Kumar; he was involved in the train attaché case exchange and turned to crime after his film career faltered.

Jatayu.description: A short, thin, and absent-minded thriller writer who uses the pen name Jatayu; he is a humorous friend and companion to Feluda.

Grand Hotel.description: A well-known hotel in Kolkata where Feluda and his companions are staying.

New Empire.description: A location near which the characters buy meetha paan; likely refers to a cinema or landmark.

Lagonda.description: An Italian car brand; here, refers to the old car in Mr Lahiri's garage.

The Ghost.description: A thriller film in which Prabeer Lahiri (Amar Kumar) plays the villain.

meetha paan.description: A sweetened betel leaf preparation, often chewed as a mouth freshener in India.

namaskar.description: A traditional Indian greeting involving folded hands.

bearer.description: A servant or attendant, often one who serves food or carries items.

Tapesh.description: Feluda's younger cousin and loyal assistant who serves as the narrator of the stories.

Sardarji.description: The taxi driver who assists Feluda and Tapesh during their late-night trip to Pretoria Street.

Rajasthan.description: A large state in northwestern India, known for its deserts and historic forts.

Nilgiris.description: A mountain range in southern India, famous for its scenic beauty and tea plantations.

North Pole.description: The northernmost point on Earth, characterized by extreme cold and snow.

The Sahara Shivers.description: A fictional book written by Lalmohan Babu, referencing the Sahara Desert.

Britannica.description: The correct name of the famous English-language encyclopedia, mistakenly referred to as 'Encyclopaedia Britannia' by Lalmohan Babu.

Darjeeling.description: A hill station in West Bengal, India, famous for its tea and scenic views.

Pretoria Street.description: A street in Calcutta where the case exchange is supposed to take place.

Birla building.description: A prominent skyscraper in Kolkata, associated with the Birla industrial family.

St Paul’s Church.description: A well-known church in Kolkata, referenced for its clock.

Marwari.description: A term referring to a member of a business community from the Marwar region of Rajasthan, often associated with trade and finance.

Balaclava helmet.description: A close-fitting woolen head covering that exposes only part of the face, commonly worn in cold climates.

galoshes.description: Waterproof overshoes worn to protect shoes from rain or snow, commonly used in India during monsoon or winter.

Puri.description: A man whose name and address are revealed to be fictitious in the course of the investigation; a friend of Dhameeja in Calcutta who was supposed to return the exchanged case.

Mr Mallik.description: A person at Sri Guru Pictures, who confirms Amar Kumar is no longer in the film.

Sparkling Stars.description: A film magazine featuring Amar Kumar's photograph.

Sri Guru Pictures.description: A film production company mentioned as making the film with Amar Kumar.

Jewel Thief.description: A famous Bollywood film starring Dev Anand, referenced for Amar Kumar's style.

Dev Anand.description: A legendary Indian film actor, known for his distinctive style.

Bentinck Street.description: A street address in Calcutta (Kolkata), where Sri Guru Pictures is located.

Janpath Hotel.description: A hotel in Delhi where reservations are made for the characters; also refers to the famous road where it is located.

Clarkes.description: A hotel in Simla where the characters are booked for four days.

England.description: Referenced as the country where the enterovioform tablets are made.

Tibet.description: A region in Asia, the subject of Shambhucharan Bose's travelogue.

divan.description: A long, low sofa without a back or arms, commonly found in Indian households.

manuscript.description: A handwritten or typed document, often referring to an unpublished literary work; 'manusprint' is a mistaken or humorous version of the word.

enterovioform.description: A medicinal tablet used for intestinal disorders, referenced as being more effective when made in England.

regulator.description: A device used to control the speed of a ceiling fan, commonly found in Indian homes.

Sawai Jai Singh.description: A historical figure, the founder of the Jantar Mantar observatory mentioned in the chapter.

Indian Airlines.description: A major Indian airline that operated domestic and international flights.

Agra Hotel.description: A hotel in Delhi where the characters consider staying.

Jantar Mantar.description: A historic astronomical observatory in Delhi, built by Sawai Jai Singh.

Prime Minister.description: The head of government in India, referenced humorously by Jatayu.

Kalka.description: A town in Haryana, India, serving as a major railway junction for trains heading to the hill station of Simla.

Frankfurt.description: A major city in Germany, referenced here as an international flight destination.

New Delhi.description: A district within Delhi, and the location of the main railway station mentioned in the chapter.

Parsee cap.description: A traditional headgear worn by members of the Parsi (Zoroastrian) community in India.

Araldite.description: A brand of strong epoxy adhesive widely used in India for bonding materials.

Kanchenjunga.description: A famous snow-capped mountain in the Himalayas, visible from Darjeeling.

Annapurna.description: A massif in the Himalayas in Nepal, renowned for its high peaks.

British.description: Refers to the colonial rulers of India before independence in 1947.

Kufri.description: A small hill station near Simla, known for its snow and scenic views.

sherpa.description: A member of an ethnic group from the Himalayas, often serving as guides or porters in mountain expeditions.

Harbilas.description: The group's driver, who recognizes the unconscious taxi driver Arvind.

Arvind.description: A taxi driver found unconscious or possibly dead in his own car blocking the road.

Australia.description: A country mentioned in relation to the boomerang, which originates from there.

Miller Gem Company.description: A jewelry store in Simla where Feluda purchased a fake stone.

Air India.description: India's national airline, mentioned in connection with an attaché case used to hide the diamond and known for giving branded gifts to passengers.

boomerang.description: A curved, flat tool from Australia, traditionally used by Indigenous Australians for hunting, which returns to the thrower.

nullah.description: A term used in India for a ravine or watercourse, often dry except during the rainy season.

Dhameeja.description: An Indian guest at the Grand Hotel from Simla, identified as the owner of the blue attaché case that gets mixed up with Dinanath Babu's.

Himachal Pradesh.description: An Indian state in the Himalayas, where Simla is located.

A Bengalee in Lamaland.description: The title of Shambhucharan's travelogue manuscript.

Lamaland.description: A term referring to Tibet or regions influenced by Tibetan Buddhism, the subject of the travelogue.

sahib.description: A term of respect or address for a man, commonly used in India.
